options.text: Each of the students have a book.
Each of the students has a book.
Each of the student have a book.
Each of the students are having a book.

items.explanation: "Each" is singular, so the verb is "has", and "of the students" keeps a plural noun.
items.shortcut: Each, every, either and neither take a singular verb.

items.body: Neither the teacher nor the students ____ present when the bell rang.
items.explanation: With neither ... nor, the verb agrees with the noun nearest to it. "Students" is plural and the sentence is in the past, so "were".
items.shortcut: Either/or and neither/nor: agree with the closer subject.

items.body: Choose the best correction of: "She is senior than me."

options.text: She is more senior than me.

items.explanation: Adjectives that come from Latin comparatives (senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior) take "to", not "than".
items.shortcut: Senior, junior, superior, inferior, prior: always followed by "to".

items.body: Choose the word closest in meaning to ABUNDANT.
items.explanation: Abundant means existing in large quantity, which is plentiful. Scarce is its opposite.
items.shortcut: Rule out the opposite first; it is usually among the options.

items.body: Choose the word most opposite in meaning to CANDID.
items.explanation: Candid means honest and straightforward. Frank, honest and open are synonyms; deceitful is the opposite.
items.shortcut: Three similar options and one outlier: the outlier is the antonym.

items.body:
Passage: Remote work removed commuting time for many employees, and several surveys found that they used part of that time to work longer. Yet the same surveys show that employees who worked fully remotely reported feeling less connected to their teams. Managers therefore began to schedule short in-person days, hoping to keep the flexibility without losing the connection.

Why did managers introduce in-person days?

options.text: To reduce the cost of office space
To keep flexibility while rebuilding team connection
To stop employees from working longer

items.explanation: The last sentence says it directly: they hoped to keep the flexibility without losing the connection.
items.shortcut: Answers to "why" questions usually sit after words such as therefore, so and because.

items.body:
Passage: Remote work removed commuting time for many employees, and several surveys found that they used part of that time to work longer. Yet the same surveys show that employees who worked fully remotely reported feeling less connected to their teams. Managers therefore began to schedule short in-person days, hoping to keep the flexibility without losing the connection.

According to the passage, what did the surveys find about fully remote employees?

options.text: They felt less connected to their teams

items.explanation: The second sentence states it: they reported feeling less connected to their teams.
items.shortcut: Detail questions are answered in the text, word for word. Do not use outside knowledge.

items.body: What does the idiom "to bite the bullet" mean?

options.text: To face an unpleasant situation with courage

items.explanation: It means to get through something difficult or unpleasant bravely, from the old practice of giving a patient a bullet to bite during surgery.
items.shortcut: Idioms are never literal. Match the feeling, not the words.

items.body: She was so tired ____ she fell asleep at her desk.
items.explanation: "So ... that" links a cause to its result.
items.shortcut: So ... that (result), as ... as (equal), more ... than (comparison).
